detail.longDescription: I'm using the Pypi JSON API to get releases information for a package; this is available at the 'detail' endpoint: https://docs.pypi.org/api/json/#get-a-project The problem is that i need each existing release number and publishing date; this is actually provided in the field 'releases' of the JSON object. However, this field is marked as deprecated since some years, so i cannot rely on it, despite that it has all the information i need. The solution proposed by the Pypi team for this case is to use Pypi index API: https://docs.pypi.org/api/index-api/#get-distributions-for-project So theoretically in this response we can have all the existing releases, each one with its publishing date. But the items don't include the version as a distinct value; it is only available from the distribution filename like in "foo_bar-42.0.tar.gz" and here is another problem because distribution filename has an old legacy and we can encounter filenames like "foo-bar-1.0.tar.gz", "foo_bar-1.0-alpha-1.tar.gz", etc.. I did not find any library that is able to correctly parse a distribution filename (with support for all the legacy) and i did not find any information from Pypi that would help to do it or to find another solution. The goal here is to find these information with the fewest request possible; actually i'm making two requests (JSON detail + Index releases) but it is not conceivable to fetch the JSON detail for each available release. Lastly, to clarify, i need to do it programmatically with Python because this is for a tool i'm working on. The purpose of this tool is to compute the project requirements lateness: given a list of requirements, for each one it resolves the version that would be installed and find the lateness of this version compared to the latest one available on Pypi.
